transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-18
Start: 09:00 AM PDT
Scheduled duration: ~45m (actual 42m)
Location: Zoom
Recorded: yes (auto)

Summary: quick show-and-tell of last week's lab results, compare latency/throughput vs incumbent provider, flagging one regression at tail latency, propose tuning steps and a dedicated slot head-to-head. Security/infra questions surfaced (VPC egress limits, KMS). Next steps: send benchmark sheet, schedule 3h run, share tuning artifacts.

Topics:
- Overview of run configuration (model variant, sequence lengths)
- P50/P95/P99 latency and throughput curves vs incumbent
- Tail latency investigation and suspected KV-cache warmup pattern
- Cost per 1M tokens comparison and tradeoffs (quant vs FP16)
- Plan for head-to-head dedicated slot test and success criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Park: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, let's do quick intros then jump into the numbers. um hi from my side is Maya, AE at Redwood, with Diego our systems engineer and Ellen from customer success.
[00:18] Liam O'Neill: hey Maya, Liam here, CTO at Calliope, and I have Priya, Jordan, and Asha with me. we've got the lab results open.
[00:24] Maya Park: great, perfect. Diego over to you for the run overview?
[00:28] Diego Ramos: yeah thanks. so quick context — this run was the week-3 sprint: model is open-7b-quant (our tuned q4a-ish quant), sequence lens sampled 128/256/512 to reflect real traffic, we did steady-state qps at 60, burst tests to 180, and inc- latency baseline run against what you called the incumbent, the which is IncumbentAI; we tried to match batching and pre-warm steps. logs and raw traces are in the sheet i shared.
[01:00] Priya Desai: quick q — open-7b-quant is the same arch you used in previous tests? we noticed different tokenization earlier.
[01:07] Diego Ramos: yes same weight family, but quantization profile tweaked — we used 4bit grouped quant with per-channel scale, that caused slightly different tokenization costs but not semantic differences. sometimes the transcriber cuts that as "for bit".
[01:21] Asha Mehta: cool — important for the latency numbers to be comparable.
[01:25] Diego Ramos: absolutely. ok metrics — p50 was 28ms vs incumbent 34ms, p95 was 110ms vs incumbent 125ms, so we're ahead on mid-tail. p99 however shows 820ms vs incumbent 640ms which is the anomaly.
[01:52] Jordan Brooks: wow p99 delta is big. what's the traffic mix during those spikes?
[01:57] Diego Ramos: when we dug in the traces, a lot of the p99 events aligned with cold KV cache misses and with occasional GC/compaction in our profiler; also a subset aligned with VPC network hiccups in eu-west zone that might be the customer's test harness bouncing ip ranges — small sample but visible.
[02:18] Liam O'Neill: is the KV cache the redwood "KV cache"? can you spell that out, we saw "K V cash" in the notes.
[02:24] Diego Ramos: sorry, KV cache — key-value cache (KV) — so per-session attention cache. warm starts avoid re-computation, cold misses can add 200-300ms. incumbent has a more aggressive prefix cache strategy in their infra which explains part of their lower p99.
[02:38] Maya Park: i also want to flag our auto-batching was tuned to keep p50 low; inc's config favors stronger tail guarantees but higher average cost. it's a tradeoff we discussed.
[02:48] Priya Desai: can we push to reduce the p99 without raising p50 more than 10%? calliope's SLO is 200ms p95 and 700ms p99 for interactive checks.
[02:59] Diego Ramos: yes, three levers: 1) prefix/KV cold-start pre-warm, 2) slightly higher batching cap (permissible for interactive bursts), 3) size-tiered serving where larger sequences route to a dedicated pool. we tested (1) and (2) in canary and saw p99 drop to ~510ms but p50 moved to 34ms.
[03:22] Priya Desai: that would meet our p95 but still tight on p99; what's the cost delta?
[03:28] Diego Ramos: rough cost delta about +7% token cost for mode with pre-warm and higher batching, mostly due to increased idle reserve and some extra compute for pre-warm. in the sheet we have cost per 1M tokens: Redwood optimized quant route $210, incumbent reported $260, headroom for tuning.
[03:46] Liam O'Neill: okay that's promising. we also care about sustained throughput (qps) under load — did you see any throughput collapse at 180 qps bursts?
[03:54] Diego Ramos: we hit a saturation point around 190 where latency increased non-linear; interestingly the incumbent spiked earlier at 160 in our lab. we think the difference is our autoscaling horizon and the dedicated GPU allocation.
[04:07] Jordan Brooks: autoscaling horizon? can you explain that a bit? we've had weird behavior on cloud autoscale before.
[04:12] Diego Ramos: sure — our serving runtime can scale within the dedicated pool quickly, but if the pool runs out of slots the fallback to shared-hosted increases latency. for the run we used a 10s scaling horizon; pushing to 5s reduces spike duration but costs more.
[04:25] Priya Desai: is that a configurable per-tenant param? we'd want control.
[04:28] Maya Park: yes, for Dedicated and for private deployments you can surface that in the runtime config. we'll include recommended defaults in the tuning doc.
[04:36] Asha Mehta: on the security side, we had a question — how are logs and traces stored? do they go to Redwood cloud by default?
[04:43] Ellen Hu: good question. by default telemetry is stored in Redwood console for hosted trials, but for Dedicated/Private you can route logs to your KMS and S3; we support customer-managed KMS and we can disable any telemetry export on request. we'll attach SOC2 and audit pack in the follow-up.
[04:58] Liam O'Neill: great — please include sample IAM policies, SAML instructions, and retention SLAs.
[05:05] Ellen Hu: will do.
[05:08] Diego Ramos: back to numbers — i want to surface one more weirdness: tail events often show a small number of tokens that balloon egress with larger alignment requests; sometimes tokenizer mismatch caused longer sequences than expected, that hit our routing thresholds and triggered a larger model path which added ~400ms. we have a mitigation to normalize tokenization across the pipeline.
[05:31] Priya Desai: so sounds like we need to align tokenization and enforce a hard seq cap so routing doesn't unexpectedly change.
[05:37] Diego Ramos: exactly. we can introduce a pre-processor step.
[05:40] Maya Park: ok moving on — we prepared a head-to-head plan. proposal: a 3-hour dedicated-slot run where we run your production traffic replay at scaled qps and compare run-to-run with incumbent. objectives: confirm p50/p95/p99, unit cost at 1M tokens, and failure modes. suggested window 10/25 1pm-4pm PT.
[06:00] Liam O'Neill: 10/25 works tentatively — need to clear with ops but favorable. what do you need from our side?
[06:07] Diego Ramos: three items: 1) traffic replay (Jordan to share), 2) whitelist IPs for dedicated slot to avoid VPC egress throttles, 3) confirm which endpoints and model variants.
[06:16] Jordan Brooks: i'll export our replay and a small script to throttle qps to mimic real patterns, will share by 10/20.
[06:23] Priya Desai: we'll confirm endpoints by 10/19 — likely chat-completions and single-turn classifier.
[06:29] Maya Park: perfect.
[06:31] Asha Mehta: curious — you mentioned quantization config and dockerfile. will that be compatible with our current on-prem test harness?
[06:38] Diego Ramos: yes, Diego: we've got both an on-prem docker snippet and a cloud executor version. the dockerfile uses the same runtime libs and a slimmed kernel optimized for grouped-4 quant. we tested on an rtx-class lab and in the cloud.
[06:52] Liam O'Neill: any red flags around model fidelity when using grouped-4? we can't accept hallucination regressions.
[06:58] Diego Ramos: fidelity loss was negligible on our evaluation set — we'll include the eval delta numbers (ROUGE, exact-match) for your prompt set in the sheet. if you need strict fidelity we can run fp16 path at higher cost.
[07:12] Priya Desai: that will be helpful.
[07:15] Maya Park: ok wrapping up technical stuff — quick recap on timeline: Diego and Maya send benchmark + tuning artifacts by 10/21; Jordan and Priya provide replay and endpoint list by 10/20/19 respectively; schedule 3h run on 10/25; post-run retrospective with raw logs within 48h.
[07:33] Liam O'Neill: one more question — SSO and audit logs for Private deployment. we want to know if we can bring our HSM.
[07:40] Ellen Hu: yes customers can bring HSM via KMIP or supported HSM connectors; we'll include the integration guide.
[07:47] Priya Desai: good.
[07:49] Jordan Brooks: also would be good to have an escalation path for 24/7 for the head-to-head.
[07:54] Maya Park: for the dedicated run we’ll provide an on-call SE and a slack channel; Diego will be primary.
[07:59] Diego Ramos: noted.
[08:02] Maya Park: any other blockers?
[08:04] Asha Mehta: none from data science side.
[08:06] Liam O'Neill: none here — thanks all.
[08:08] Maya Park: awesome. i'll follow up with the sheet and pins. thanks everyone and talk soon.

End of transcript.
